proposed.explanation: Your overriding need is to raise 10,000 EGP in cash within 3 months for a family wedding, and your risk tolerance is low. Your total portfolio is only 5,080 EGP (1,000 EGP cash + 200 × 20.40 = 4,080 EGP in EFID). Even selling all 200 EFID shares brings you to 5,080 EGP, which is still 4,920 EGP short of your target. Because you need the cash on a fixed 3-month deadline and cannot afford a loss, holding the shares exposes you to price risk you cannot absorb. Selling all 200 shares is the most responsible step to maximise your available cash. Please note that even after this sale you will still be short of the 10,000 EGP you need; you will have to identify an additional source of funds (savings, family support, etc.) to cover the remaining 4,920 EGP gap. The company's fundamentals are solid—FY2025 revenue grew to 20.92 billion EGP from 16.15 billion, and net profit rose to 2.70 billion EGP from 1.61 billion, with EPS doubling to 2.18 EGP—but a 3-month wedding deadline and low loss tolerance make the investment case secondary to your liquidity need. This is guidance, not a guarantee; share prices can move in either direction over the next few weeks, so selling sooner rather than later reduces that uncertainty.

claims.statement: EFID consolidated revenue for the year ended 31 December 2025 was 20,915,072,432 EGP.
EFID consolidated revenue for the year ended 31 December 2024 was 16,146,545,699 EGP.
EFID consolidated net profit for the year ended 31 December 2025 was 2,695,301,670 EGP.
EFID consolidated net profit for the year ended 31 December 2024 was 1,606,727,698 EGP.
EFID basic and diluted EPS for the year ended 31 December 2025 was 2.18 EGP.
EFID basic and diluted EPS for the year ended 31 December 2024 was 1.09 EGP.

limitations: The evidence covers only EFID's FY2025 and FY2024 consolidated financials; there is no information on dividend policy, share liquidity, or near-term price outlook.
The investor's total portfolio (5,080 EGP) is below the 10,000 EGP cash target, so no combination of portfolio actions alone can meet the full requirement.
No AMBIGUOUS figures were present in the evidence.
